sthana_desc: Articulated at the throat and soft palate. The back of the tongue lightly touches the velum.
anatomical_tip: Keep the tongue tip relaxed behind lower teeth; press the back of your tongue against the soft palate without releasing an air burst.

sthana_desc: Articulated at the soft palate with a strong puff of breath (Mahāprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Pronounce like 'क' but release an energetic burst of breath (aspirated) from the throat.

sthana_desc: Voiced velar stop. Vocal cords vibrate; gentle breath release.
anatomical_tip: Vibrate your vocal cords at the throat with minimal breath exhalation (Alpaprāṇa).

sthana_desc: Voiced aspirated velar stop. Strong vocal vibration combined with deep breath.
anatomical_tip: Deep resonant sound from the throat with vocal vibration followed by a heavy warm breath release.

sthana_desc: Velar nasal. Air resonates through both the throat and nasal cavity.
anatomical_tip: Tongue back blocks velum while air resonates freely through the nasal cavity (as in 'sing').

sthana_desc: Articulated by raising the middle blade of the tongue firmly against the hard palate.
anatomical_tip: Flatten the middle of your tongue against the roof of mouth (hard palate). Do not round lips.

sthana_desc: Palatal stop with strong aspiration (Mahāprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Middle of tongue on hard palate, released with an explosive puff of air.

sthana_desc: Voiced palatal stop with minimal breath (Alpaprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Vocal cords vibrate while tongue middle touches the hard palate.

sthana_desc: Voiced palatal stop with heavy aspiration (Mahāprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Tongue middle on palate; vocal vibration combined with heavy puff of air.

sthana_desc: Palatal nasal sound resonating in the nasal cavity.
anatomical_tip: Tongue middle touches palate while air flows smoothly through the nose (as in Spanish 'año').

sthana_desc: Articulated by curling the tip of the tongue up and back against the dome (mūrdhā) of the palate.
anatomical_tip: Curl tongue tip backwards towards the high arched roof of mouth, tap once cleanly. Never touch teeth!

sthana_desc: Retroflex stop with forceful aspiration (Mahāprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Tongue curled back to palate roof; release with a sharp burst of breath.

sthana_desc: Voiced retroflex stop with gentle breath (Alpaprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Vibrate vocal cords as curled tongue tip taps the high palate roof.

sthana_desc: Voiced retroflex stop with strong aspiration (Mahāprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Curled tongue on high roof with vocal vibration and heavy breath exhalation.

sthana_desc: Retroflex nasal consonant resonating through nasal passage.
anatomical_tip: Curl tongue tip backward against palate roof while letting sound resonate in nasal chamber.

sthana_desc: Articulated by placing the flat tip of the tongue directly against the upper front teeth.
anatomical_tip: CRITICAL: Place the flat tip of your tongue against the back of your upper teeth (like Italian 'pasta'), NOT curled back on the roof!

sthana_desc: Dental stop with strong aspiration (Mahāprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Tongue tip touches back of upper teeth, releasing a distinct puff of air.

sthana_desc: Voiced dental stop with soft breath (Alpaprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Vocal cords vibrate while tongue tip touches the back of upper teeth.

sthana_desc: Voiced dental stop with heavy breath (Mahāprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Tongue tip touches upper teeth; vocal resonance combined with warm breath discharge.

sthana_desc: Dental nasal consonant resonating through nasal passage.
anatomical_tip: Tongue tip touches back of upper teeth while air escapes freely through the nose.

sthana_desc: Articulated by bringing the upper and lower lips firmly together.
anatomical_tip: Press lips together and release cleanly without aspiration or voicing.

sthana_desc: Bilabial aspirated stop. Lips close and release with a burst of air (NOT English 'f').
anatomical_tip: CRITICAL: Do NOT use teeth like English 'f'! Keep both lips touching and release with a strong puff of air.

sthana_desc: Voiced bilabial stop with gentle breath (Alpaprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Lips close and open with vocal cord vibration and minimal breath.

sthana_desc: Voiced bilabial stop with heavy breath (Mahāprāṇa).
anatomical_tip: Vocal cords vibrate while lips release with an energetic warm breath.

sthana_desc: Bilabial nasal consonant resonating through nasal passage.
anatomical_tip: Lips closed together while sound resonates inside the nasal cavity.

sthana_desc: Antastha (semivowel) produced with middle of tongue raised toward hard palate.
anatomical_tip: Glide the tongue body toward hard palate smoothly without full friction.

sthana_desc: Retroflex semivowel. Tongue tip taps slightly behind the alveolar ridge.
anatomical_tip: Tongue tip vibrates quickly against the dome of the palate.

sthana_desc: Dental semivowel. Tongue tip against upper teeth while air escapes on both sides.
anatomical_tip: Touch upper teeth with tongue tip, letting air flow smoothly along both sides.

sthana_desc: Labiodental semivowel. Upper teeth gently contact the inner edge of lower lip.
anatomical_tip: Upper teeth lightly brush lower lip while vocal cords hum; smoother than English 'v'.

sthana_desc: Palatal fricative. Tongue blade spreads flat against the hard palate.
anatomical_tip: Spread tongue flat along hard palate roof (as in 'Śiva' / 'Śānti'). Softer hiss than retroflex 'ष'.

sthana_desc: Retroflex sibilant. Tongue tip curled backward to the dome of the palate.
anatomical_tip: CRITICAL: Curl tongue tip backward towards roof of mouth (as in 'Kṛṣṇa' / 'Puruṣa'). Deep, hollow friction.

sthana_desc: Dental sibilant. Tongue tip placed directly behind upper front teeth.
anatomical_tip: Crisp hiss with tongue tip close to upper front teeth (as in 'Satya' / 'Sūrya').

sthana_desc: Glottal aspirate voiced fricative directly from the throat.
anatomical_tip: Deep unhindered voiced exhalation emerging from the throat/glottis.

sthana_desc: Short central vowel uttered with throat open and neutral mouth posture.
anatomical_tip: Relax tongue in center of floor of mouth; open throat comfortably.

sthana_desc: Long open throat vowel with mouth fully opened (2 mātrās).
anatomical_tip: Open mouth wide vertically, voice resonates deeply from the throat.

sthana_desc: Short high front vowel; tongue arches toward hard palate.
anatomical_tip: Raise front middle of tongue toward hard palate with corners of mouth slightly widened.

sthana_desc: Long high front vowel held for 2 mātrās near hard palate.
anatomical_tip: Close palatal posture held for 2 full beats with clear vocal pitch.

sthana_desc: Short high back vowel; lips rounded comfortably.
anatomical_tip: Round the lips forward like a small circle without touching teeth.

sthana_desc: Long high back vowel held for 2 mātrās with rounded lips.
anatomical_tip: Tightly rounded lips held for two full beats.

sthana_desc: Vocalic 'r'; tip of tongue raised toward the dome of the palate.
anatomical_tip: Curl tongue tip lightly toward dome of palate and voice continuously as a pure vowel (not 'ri').

sthana_desc: Diphthongal vowel articulated jointly at the throat and hard palate (pure long 'e').
anatomical_tip: Open throat while raising tongue blade midway to hard palate.

sthana_desc: Complex vowel transitioning from open throat to palatal glide.
anatomical_tip: Start at open throat 'a' and glide smoothly up towards 'i'.

sthana_desc: Vowel articulated jointly at the throat with rounded lips.
anatomical_tip: Open throat with medium rounded lips (pure long 'o').

sthana_desc: Complex vowel transitioning from open throat to rounded lips.
anatomical_tip: Start from throat 'a' and round lips smoothly toward 'u'.
